segments: The tenth dynasty:
The Arab kings.
also Ibn 'Addas,
may their memory be for a curse!
And there was rest for the Muslims and the Christians.
And in their place was appointed as chief proxiros a Christian man,
whose name was Mansur ibn 'Abdun.
This man was envied by the grandees,
and they slandered him,
and on his account persecution arose against the Christians.
And many of the clerks were tortured until they died,
and were thrown to the dogs.
And Mansur himself was also beaten until he was thought to be dead,
and was thrown to the dogs.
And when it was found that he was moving a little,
he was carried and brought to his house, and he recovered.
And again the Caliph restored him to his post,
and gave him the title of al-Kafi,
that is, 'the capable' {or 'the sufficient'}.
It is said of al-Hakim
that this whole [city] was terrified and afraid of him,
so that people were completely relieved from evildoers,
and no one at night would lock his shop.
And al-Hakim would ride at night on an Egyptian donkey and go around the streets,
and no one dared to stand up or to bow down to him.
And lamps would shine all night long,
and the night in Egypt was like daytime in his days.
And in the year 392
of the Arabs [1001-1002 AD],
the Muslims rioted against the Christians in Baghdad,
and plundered their houses,
and stretched forth their hands also against the churches to destroy them.
And when they set fire to that Jacobite church which is in the Flour Quarter (Qati'at al-Daqiq),
it fell upon a multitude of the zealous men, women, and youths, and suffocated them,
and burned the burners;
and they became a terror to the onlookers.
And after a year, abundant locusts appeared in the region of Mosul and Baghdad,
and it was very severe in Shiraz.
It left no grass, nor leaves on the trees,
to such an extent that it even consumed the pieces of cloth that the fullers were bleaching,
and from each piece of cloth the fuller gave only a patch to its owner.
And there was famine,
and a kor of wheat was sold in Baghdad for one hundred and twenty gold dinars.
And fiery pillars appeared in the sky,
from the north pole to the middle of the sky.
And in the year 396
[1005-1006 AD], a star was seen that resembled Aphrodite (Venus) in size and brightness,
in the zodiacal sign of Scorpio (or Aries),
and its rays rolled along, and it gave light like the moon.
And it remained for four months,
and vanished.
And in the year
